section: Government of India Act 1919 - dyarchy, Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms; Rowlatt Act
subsections: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate
GoI Act 1919 - sections and bodies, first ministries
Direct elections - first Act and franchise

accepted.s: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were named after which two officials?
accepted.x: The reforms were named after Edwin Montagu, the Secretary of State for India, and Lord Chelmsford, the Viceroy of India.
accepted.tq: Use the name-to-office association to distinguish similarly named constitutional reforms.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report was announced in which month and year?
accepted.x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report was announced in July 1918; it subsequently formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919.
accepted.tq: Separate the report date from the declaration date and the Act date.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional status of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms?
o: They were rules framed exclusively by the Viceroy's Executive Council.
They were recommendations of the Indian National Congress alone.
They were an Act of the UK Parliament.
They were a royal proclamation establishing the Chamber of Princes.
accepted.x: The Montagu-Chelmsford proposals were enacted through the Government of India Act, 1919, an Act of the UK Parliament.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct constitutional source instead of confusing proposals with executive rules.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919, consider the following statements:
1. It was introduced in the provinces.
2. It divided provincial subjects into reserved and transferred subjects.
3. It made the provincial budget independent of the central budget.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces, provincial subjects were divided into reserved and transferred categories, and the provincial budget was separated from the central budget.
accepted.tq: Check whether each feature belongs to provincial dyarchy rather than to the later provincial autonomy scheme.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Reserved subjects — Governor and Executive Council — not answerable to the legislature
Reserved subjects — elected ministers — answerable to the legislature
Transferred subjects — Governor alone — not answerable to the legislature
Transferred subjects — Secretary of State — answerable to Parliament only
accepted.x: Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor and his Executive Council and were not answerable to the provincial legislature.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair linking reserved subjects with the Governor and Executive Council.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Under the dyarchical arrangement, which of the following were transferred subjects?
1. Education
2. Health
3. Local self-government
4. Law and order
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Education, health and local self-government were transferred subjects administered by ministers responsible to the legislature. Law and order was a reserved subject.
accepted.tq: Find the one reserved subject and eliminate the option that includes it.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A provincial minister responsible to the elected legislature was most likely to administer which of the following under the Government of India Act, 1919?
accepted.x: Education was a transferred subject administered by a Governor's minister drawn from the elected legislature and answerable to it.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional relationship to identify a transferred subject.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The central legislature under the Government of India Act, 1919 was:
o: Bicameral, consisting of the Chamber of Princes and the Federal Court
Bicameral, consisting of the Council of State and the Legislative Assembly
Unicameral, consisting only of nominated members
Tricameral, consisting of the Council of State, Legislative Assembly and Provincial Council
accepted.x: The Act introduced a bicameral central legislature comprising the Council of State as the upper chamber and the Legislative Assembly as the lower chamber.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional arrangement with the exact names of its two chambers.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the central legislature under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. The Legislative Assembly had 145 members.
2. Of the members of the Legislative Assembly, 104 were elected.
3. The Council of State had 60 members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Legislative Assembly had 145 members, including 104 elected members, while the Council of State had 60 members.
accepted.tq: Verify each numerical detail separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, how many members of the Viceroy's Executive Council, excluding the Commander-in-Chief, were to be Indians?
accepted.x: Three of the six members of the Viceroy's Executive Council, other than the Commander-in-Chief, were to be Indians.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the specified six-member group from the separately excluded Commander-in-Chief.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following communities were included when communal representation was extended under the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms?
1. Sikhs
2. Indian Christians
3. Anglo-Indians
4. Europeans
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Communal representation was extended beyond Muslims to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.
accepted.tq: Treat the complete community list as a composition question and check every member.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The franchise under the Government of India Act, 1919 was primarily based on:
o: Religious identity and nomination by the Governor
accepted.x: The franchise remained limited and was based on qualifications relating to property, taxation and education.
accepted.tq: Reject the universal-suffrage trap and identify the three stated qualifications.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: Direct elections to the central legislature
Creation of the office of High Commissioner for India in London
Separation of provincial budgets from the central budget
Provincial autonomy in place of dyarchy
accepted.x: Provincial autonomy was associated with the Government of India Act, 1935. The 1919 Act introduced dyarchy in the provinces, along with the other listed features.
accepted.tq: Use the later 1935 feature as the chronological trap in a NOT question.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The gradual introduction of responsible government in India was associated with the declaration of:
accepted.x: Montagu's August Declaration of 20 August 1917 stated the policy of the gradual introduction of responsible government in India.
accepted.tq: Separate the August Declaration date from the later report and reform dates.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The provision for establishing a Public Service Commission in India was contained in which section of the Government of India Act, 1919?
accepted.x: Section 96(C) of the Government of India Act, 1919 provided for the establishment of a Public Service Commission in India.
accepted.tq: Use exact-section recall, a common constitutional-provision trap.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1919 - sections and bodies, first ministries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Public Service Commission provided for under the Government of India Act, 1919 was set up on:
accepted.x: The Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926, after the Lee Commission.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the statutory provision in 1919 from the body's establishment in 1926.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1919 - sections and bodies, first ministries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was created under the Government of India Act, 1919 as a consultative body of Indian rulers?
accepted.x: The Chamber of Princes, also known as Narendra Mandal, was created as a consultative body of rulers under the 1919 reforms.
accepted.tq: Match the body's function with its institutional identity rather than its legislative name.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1919 - sections and bodies, first ministries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Chamber of Princes, or Narendra Mandal, was set up in:
accepted.x: The Chamber of Princes was set up in 1921 by royal proclamation under the framework of the 1919 reforms.
accepted.tq: Keep the reform year distinct from the year in which the associated body was established.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1919 - sections and bodies, first ministries  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Office-holder)
a. Frederick Whyte
a. Sachchidananda Sinha
c. Vithalbhai Patel
List-II (Position)
i. First elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly
ii. First Deputy President
iii. First President

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Frederick Whyte was the first President, Sachchidananda Sinha the first Deputy President, and Vithalbhai Patel the first elected Indian President.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive pair Vithalbhai Patel–first elected Indian President and complete the matching.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1919 - sections and bodies, first ministries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who became the first elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly in 1925?
accepted.x: Vithalbhai Patel became the first elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly in 1925.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first office-holder from the first elected Indian holder of the office.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1919 - sections and bodies, first ministries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Frederick Whyte and Sachchidananda Sinha were respectively associated with which offices?
o: First elected Indian President and first Chief Minister of Madras
First President and first Deputy President of the Legislative Assembly
High Commissioner for India and first President of the Legislative Assembly
First Deputy President and first President of the Council of State
accepted.x: Frederick Whyte was the first President and Sachchidananda Sinha was the first Deputy President of the Legislative Assembly.
accepted.tq: Separate similar office-holder facts by matching each person to the exact office and status.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1919 - sections and bodies, first ministries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the Madras elections of 1920, which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: Congress boycotted the elections and the Justice Party won 63 seats
The Justice Party boycotted the elections and Congress won 63 seats
Both Congress and the Justice Party boycotted the elections
accepted.x: The Congress boycotted the 1920 Madras elections as part of the Non-Cooperation movement, while the Justice Party won 63 seats.
accepted.tq: Pair the political action with the correct party and election result.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1919 - sections and bodies, first ministries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Justice Party held office in Madras for most of which period?
accepted.x: The Justice Party held office in Madras for most of the period from 1920 to 1937.
accepted.tq: Use the complete period rather than confusing it with the first ministry's starting year.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1919 - sections and bodies, first ministries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections on the basis of:
o: Separate nomination by the Secretary of State
accepted.x: The Act introduced direct elections, but the franchise remained limited by property, tax and educational qualifications.
accepted.tq: Combine the electoral method with the qualification-based nature of the franchise.
accepted.sec: Direct elections - first Act and franchise  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Act introduced elected non-official members, largely through indirect and separate electorates?
accepted.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 introduced elected non-official members, largely through indirect and separate electorates. Direct elections were associated with the 1919 Act.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the 1909 indirect electoral innovation and the 1919 direct elections.
accepted.sec: Direct elections - first Act and franchise  [APPSC]

accepted.s: If an examination question asks for the first Act associated with direct elections in India, which answer is most appropriate?
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections. The 1909 Act introduced elected non-official members mainly through indirect and separate electorates.
accepted.tq: Resolve a close-option ambiguity by distinguishing direct elections from indirect elections.
accepted.sec: Direct elections - first Act and franchise  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match the following Acts with their principal features:
List-I (Act)
a. Regulating Act
b. Pitt's India Act
c. Indian Councils Act, 1909
d. Government of India Act, 1919
List-II (Feature)
i. Provincial dyarchy and central bicameralism
ii. Board of Control and dual control
iii. Governor-General of Bengal and Supreme Court at Calcutta
iv. Separate electorate for Muslims

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Regulating Act, 1773 provided for the Governor-General of Bengal and the Supreme Court at Calcutta; Pitt's India Act created the Board of Control; the 1909 Act introduced Muslim separate electorates; and the 1919 Act introduced dyarchy and central bicameralism.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair Regulating Act–Supreme Court at Calcutta and eliminate mismatched codes.
accepted.sec: Act/reform → year and feature  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pitt's India Act, 1784 — Board of Control
Regulating Act, 1773 — Supreme Court at Calcutta
Morley-Minto Reforms, 1909 — separate electorate for Muslims
accepted.x: The 1919 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy, not provincial autonomy. Provincial autonomy was a feature of the Government of India Act, 1935.
accepted.tq: Identify the later constitutional feature wrongly brought into the 1919 framework.
accepted.sec: Act/reform → year and feature  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Act is correctly associated with the introduction of dyarchy in the provinces, bicameralism at the Centre and direct elections?
accepted.x: These three features were introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919, also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
accepted.tq: Recognize the characteristic three-feature combination of the 1919 Act.
accepted.sec: Act/reform → year and feature  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Councils Act, 1909 is associated with separate electorates for Muslims.
2. The Government of India Act, 1919 is associated with dyarchy in the provinces.
3. The Government of India Act, 1935 prescribed a federation and provincial autonomy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the 1909 Act introduced Muslim separate electorates, the 1919 Act introduced provincial dyarchy, and the 1935 Act provided for federation and provincial autonomy.
accepted.tq: Map each Act to its signature feature and test the sequence across reforms.
accepted.sec: Act/reform → year and feature  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the 1909 and 1919 reforms?
o: The 1919 reforms abolished communal representation introduced in 1909.
The 1909 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy, whereas the 1919 reforms introduced Muslim separate electorates.
The 1909 reforms introduced Muslim separate electorates, whereas the 1919 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy and direct elections.
Both reforms introduced provincial autonomy in the provinces.
accepted.x: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims, while the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 introduced provincial dyarchy and direct elections.
accepted.tq: Compare the signature feature of each reform instead of swapping their dates and provisions.
accepted.sec: Act/reform → year and feature  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who is associated with the description 'Father of the Communal Electorate'?
accepted.x: Lord Minto is associated with the title 'Father of the Communal Electorate' because the Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
accepted.tq: Link the popular epithet to the reform and Viceroy of the same period.
accepted.sec: Act/reform → year and feature  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The office of High Commissioner for India in London was created by the:
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 created the office of High Commissioner for India in London.
accepted.tq: Match the institutional office with the constitutional Act that created it.
accepted.sec: GoI Act 1919 - sections and bodies, first ministries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the initial location of the simultaneous ICS examination in India?
accepted.x: From 1922, the ICS examination was held simultaneously in India at Allahabad and was later conducted at Delhi.
accepted.tq: Test the sequence of locations rather than recalling only the year.
accepted.sec: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms - dyarchy, subjects, central legislature, electorate  [APPSC]
